summary: Both sides render the same pattern — a handful of evenly-hued glowing 'flies' wandering a dark 16x16 canvas — but the port draws 6 flies instead of 7, gives each a tighter/dimmer glow, and its flies spend ~61% of their time pinned crawling along the canvas border versus the original's ~39%.
observations: Neither side exposes any control (probe: 'no settable controls' on orig and port). Control surfaces match.

Both sides are steady over long windows: 60 s survey and 240 s / 2 fps extended survey both show one regime, no mode rotation, no palette walk, brightnessTrend 'steady' on both; a --skip 200 window is indistinguishable in character from t=0. Orig mean brightness ~3.0, port ~2.4 in every window measured.

FLY COUNT / HUE SET (the headline structural difference). Orig always renders 7 flies whose hues sit exactly on k/7 (measured RGB hues 0.000, 0.143, 0.286, 0.429, 0.571, 0.714, 0.857). Port always renders 6 flies on k/6 (0.000, 0.167, 0.333, 0.500, 0.667, 0.833). Confirmed at seeds 1, 7 and 1234, at wall clocks spanning a full day, and at grids 8x8 / 16x16 / 32x32 / 32x8 — the counts never change on either side.

The two sides agree on where the flies START. At seed 1 / 16x16 t=0 both put a red fly at (8,6) v255, a k=1 fly at (12,8) v96, a k=4 fly at (11,5) v~169 and a k=5 fly at (6,5) v117; flies 2, 3 and the orig-only 7th differ. Same coincidence at seed 7, seed 1234, and at 32x32 (both put fly0 at (17,12) v160). So the port reproduces the original's spawn logic and just instantiates one fewer fly.

GLOW KERNEL. At --grid 32x32, t=0, the port's fly0 is EXACTLY the 4-pixel core of the original's fly0 with byte-identical values ((-1,0)=153 (0,0)=160 (-1,1)=119 (0,1)=123); the original adds a surrounding dimmer ring ((-1,-1)=65 (0,-1)=67 (-2,0)=54 (1,0)=58 (-2,1)=46 (-1,2)=40) for 10 lit px and total value ~885 vs the port's 555-710 over 4-6 px. Same on the default 16x16: orig red fly at t=0.20 is a 5-px plus (255/29/26/25/22, sum 357), port red at t=0.25 is 3 px (200/41/27, sum 268). Visually the original's flies are soft dots with a halo; the port's are harder small blocks.

EDGE BEHAVIOUR (the most visible motion difference). Over a 120 s / 20 fps positional sample, the fraction of fly-time spent within 1 px of a border is 0.453 (orig) vs 0.668 (port); over a separate 60 s run with a 0.6 px edge band it is 0.390 vs 0.610. Column histograms: orig x=0/x=15 hold 9.6%/12.0% of fly-time against ~5.5% interior; port x=0/x=15 hold 15.3%/17.6% and its y=0 row alone holds 21.0%. Trajectory dumps at 0.1 s over t=60..75 s show a port fly pinned at x=15.0 for the entire 8 s printed while sliding up and down the right wall, and a second pinned at y=0.0 for ~7 s; the original's flies touch a wall for ~0.6-1.5 s at a time and then head back into the field.

SPEED. 60 s / 20 fps centroid tracking on the default 16x16 rig: orig mean 8.48 px/s (percentiles p25/p50/p75 = 1.02/5.49/17.27), port mean 5.86 px/s (1.92/4.35/9.22). Restricting to samples away from the border: orig mean 9.66 px/s (median exactly 10.00 = 1 px per 0.1 s), port mean 7.76 px/s (median 7.26). So the port is ~20-25% slower in free flight and ~30% slower overall once wall dwell is counted.

MOTION CADENCE. The original advances in discrete hops: at --fps 20 adjacent captured frames are byte-identical in strict alternation (zeroMotionFrames 61/120), at --fps 40 identical in runs of 3 (161/240, transitions every 0.075 s), at --fps 10 every frame differs. The port updates every frame (zeroMotionFrames 12/120 at 20 fps). Over long lags both sides are fps-invariant (orig median displacement at tau=1 s: 3.89/3.93/3.77 px at 10/20/40 fps; port 20 fps and 40 fps give byte-identical MSD curves 0.54/1.00/2.33/3.10/4.45), so neither is frame-rate coupled at 20-40 fps; the port is ~30% slower at 10 fps than at 20/40, the original is not.
Both sides saturate to the same confinement scale: median displacement plateaus near 4.5 px at tau = 2 s on a 16x16 grid, i.e. both are confined random walks, not ballistic drifters.

CLOCK: --wall-clock swept over 1755977000, 1756000000, 1756014000, 1756036800, 1756050000 (a full day of times) produced byte-identical renders on BOTH sides at t=0 and t=1 s. Despite the slug name, nothing observable in either side is time-of-day driven, so the known engine gap (hour/minute builtins pinned) has no differential impact here.

RESOLUTION: both sides scale fly glow size with the grid (fly footprint grows from 1-3 px at 16x16 to 4-10 px at 32x32 on both) and keep their own fly count fixed, so neither is index-only and both behave the same way under grid changes. At 8x8 both sides dim to the point where some flies fall below 8-bit quantisation (orig showed 4-6 visible, port 2-6).
Neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both); neither errors at compile or runtime in any of ~25 runs.
feedback: Add the seventh fly. The original always draws 7 flies with hues at k/7 (0, 1/7, 2/7 ... 6/7); the port draws 6 at k/6. Fixing the count also fixes the hue spacing — the port's palette is currently the six pure R/Y/G/C/B/M primaries while the original's is seven off-primary hues.

Widen the fly glow by one pixel of falloff. The port renders only the bright 2x2 core of each fly (it is byte-identical to the original's core), while the original surrounds that core with a dimmer ring at roughly 25-40% of core brightness — at 32x32 the original's fly covers ~10 px / total value ~885, the port's ~4-6 px / ~555-710. This is why whole-rig mean brightness is 2.4 (port) vs 3.0 (orig) even before the missing fly is counted.

Fix the edge/boundary handling — this is the biggest visual divergence. The port's flies get stuck against the wall: measured over 60-120 s they sit within a pixel of the border 61-67% of the time (original 39-45%), and a 0.1 s trajectory dump caught one port fly pinned at x=15 for a continuous 8 s and another at y=0 for ~7 s, sliding along the wall. The original's flies contact a wall for only ~0.6-1.5 s before turning back into the field. It looks like the port clamps the position at the boundary without turning the fly around, so an outward-heading fly keeps pressing on the wall until its own wander eventually reverses.

Speed the flies up ~25%. In free flight (away from the border) the original's flies move at a median 10.0 px/s on a 16x16 grid (mean 9.66); the port's median is 7.26 px/s (mean 7.76). Overall means including wall dwell are 8.48 vs 5.86 px/s.

Cosmetic/optional: the original's motion is quantised — its whole frame is byte-identical for 2 rendered frames at 20 fps and 3 at 40 fps, i.e. the flies hop about 10-13 times a second rather than gliding. The port updates every frame and therefore looks smoother than the original. Both are fps-invariant in net travel at 20-40 fps, so this is a texture-of-motion difference, not a timing bug; match it only if the stutter is wanted.

Do NOT chase the wall clock: both sides render byte-identically across a full day of --wall-clock values, so nothing here is clock-driven and the pinned time-of-day builtins are not a factor for this slug.
